sn8.2:1.1: MS edition inserts a _… pe…_ here indicating an abbreviation. This is the only occurrence of this pattern in the Suttas.
sn8.2:3.4: The unique term _mutattā_ (“who understand themselves”) recalls Yājñavalkya, “when the Self is seen, heard, thought, cognized” (_ātmani khalv are dṛṣṭe śrute mate vijñāta_, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.5.6).
sn8.2:4.2: In line with the Abhidhammic understanding that _muta_ means “experienced through smelling, tasting, and touching”, the commentator explains that _paṭigha_ here means smell and taste, while _muta_ means touch. The commentary to the same line at [thag21:8.2]() says the opposite: _paṭigha_ is touch, while _muta_ is taste and smell. The solution is to take the grammar and meaning of the line literally. The line is divided in two by _ca_, and _paṭigha_ is a noun qualified by the two past participles in the first clause. This fits its regular meaning of any kind of “impingement” contact through the physical senses ([dn15:20.4](), [mn77:22.8](), [sn1.23:4.3]()). _Muta_ is separate, as “thought” is experienced via “labeling” ([dn15:20.2]()), not by “impingement”.
sn8.2:5.1: Presumably an abbreviated reference to the sixty-two views of the Brahmajalasutta ([dn1]()), which is referenced as “sixty-three” at [snp3.6:42.1]()).
